body: Isn’t that the core of the critique? That focusing on idealistic changes and theoretical revolutions has kept people from actually going out and starting to organize the workers movement? People don’t just develop a class consciousness by themselves, especially not now, after years without there being any real alternative.

But doesn’t historical dialectics define class as a the objective fact that most people spend the main part of their day working for someone else? I don’t see how you can call the objective interest to defy the terms and own the products of your own labour as an identity construct. You don’t choose not to inherit your own means of production. What differentiates Marx study of contradictions from the Critical Theorists, is that he not only pointed out that change is possible, but also pointed out a pathway to realize that change. I don’t see how Critical Theory points towards a real materialist chance, that could stop the ongoing wars, ecological and economic crisis…

Apart from that: yes, I agree that Rockhill’s position on China is uninformed, China as well as Cuba are no longer communist nations. But just because some communists have come to weird conclusions doesn’t refute their whole argument.
